"ROLE
You are a senior mobile game developer, game designer, and pixel artist. Build a complete medieval grand-strategy game for MOBILE inspired by the Total War genre (turn-based campaign map + real-time tactical battles). Use ORIGINAL names, factions, lore, art, and audio. Do not copy any existing game's assets, names, or UI.

PROJECT TITLE: \"Crown @COMMENT_BODY@ Banner\" (placeholder)

PLATFORM @COMMENT_BODY@ TECH
- Target: Android and iOS phones and tablets (landscape orientation)
- Engine: Godot 4 (2D) or Unity 2D, exportable to APK/AAB and iOS
- 100% touch controls. No keyboard or mouse required
- Must run smoothly at 30-60 FPS on mid-range phones (4GB RAM)
- Modular, clean, commented code. Separate data (JSON) from logic
- Must run immediately. Provide setup steps, project structure, build/export guide, and README

=====================================
1. ART DIRECTION: REALISTIC PIXEL ART
=====================================
- Detailed high-resolution pixel art (HD pixel art), NOT cartoonish or chibi
- Realistic proportions: units are 3-4 heads tall, not oversized heads
- Muted, natural medieval palette (earth tones, steel grey, dark reds), limited to 32-64 colors per sprite
- Dynamic lighting and soft shadows on pixel sprites (normal maps or shader-based lighting), day/night and weather lighting
- Detailed armor, weapons, banners, and cloth shading per faction; visible silhouettes that tell unit types apart at a glance
- 8-direction sprite animation: idle, walk, run, attack, block, hit, death, rout
- Battlefield: top-down or slight isometric 2.5D pixel terrain with grass, mud, snow, rivers, forests, hills, castles with realistic textures
- Campaign map: pixel-art parchment map with terrain, seasonal changes (snow in winter, green in summer), animated banners and armies
- Particles in pixel style: dust, arrows, fire, smoke, rain, snow, stylized hit effects (gore toggle optional)
- Consistent pixel grid (no mixed pixel sizes), no blur, nearest-neighbor filtering
- All art original; placeholder assets must be replaceable

=====================================
2. SETTING @COMMENT_BODY@ FACTIONS
=====================================
- Fictional medieval continent, 5 playable factions:
  1. Heavy-infantry feudal kingdom (strong defense)
  2. Horse-lord steppe empire (fast cavalry, weak cities)
  3. Mountain clans (spearmen, ambushes, forest/hill bonuses)
  4. Merchant republic (wealth, mercenaries, navy)
  5. Crusading order (elite knights, high morale, low income)
- Each faction: unique banner, color, starting region, 2 unique units, 1 passive bonus, short lore intro

=====================================
3. CAMPAIGN MAP (turn-based)
=====================================
- 20-25 provinces, each with a capital and 0-2 minor settlements
- Terrain: plains, forest, hills, mountains, coast, river
- Fog of war, movement range, zones of control, passes, bridges
- Seasons (1 turn = 1 season): winter slows movement and reduces food
- Random events: plague, harvest, rebellion, bandits, famine, festival
- Tap to select, tap destination to move, pinch to zoom, drag to pan, long-press for info

Settlements @COMMENT_BODY@ buildings (tiered)
- Town center (levels 1-5), barracks, archery range, stables, siege workshop, farm, market, port, mine, blacksmith, church, tavern, walls, watchtower
- Build queues, construction time, upkeep

Economy
- Gold, food, wood, iron; population growth, public order, tax levels
- Army upkeep, trade routes, tribute, loot, ransom, bankruptcy and starvation effects

Armies @COMMENT_BODY@ characters
- Generals: stats (command, tactics, siege, charisma), traits, loyalty, XP, skill tree, aging/death
- Army stack limit (16 units), supply, attrition, replenishment
- Agents: spy, diplomat, merchant
- Recruit, merge, split, garrison, disband

Diplomacy
- Alliances, non-aggression pacts, trade, vassalage, tribute, marriage, war/peace
- AI attitude score with a clear explanation

Tech tree
- 3 branches (Military, Economy, Society), 30+ techs

Win/Lose
- Win: control 12 provinces including 3 great cities, or eliminate all rivals
- Lose: lose all settlements or king dies without heir
- Difficulty: easy, normal, hard, legendary

=====================================
4. REAL-TIME BATTLES (touch-optimized)
=====================================
Controls
- Tap to select a regiment, drag on ground to set move destination
- Drag a line to set formation width and facing
- Two-finger drag to pan, pinch to zoom, two-finger twist to rotate (optional)
- Bottom toolbar with big touch buttons: attack, hold, charge, retreat, skirmish, fire at will, formation
- Multi-select via lasso (hold and draw), control groups via on-screen buttons
- Pause, slow motion, 1x/2x speed buttons
- Auto-resolve option with predicted outcome
- Haptic feedback on charges and impacts (toggleable)

Unit types (regiments of 20-100 soldiers)
- Infantry: militia, sword @COMMENT_BODY@ shield, halberdiers, elite guards
- Spearmen: levy spears, pike phalanx
- Ranged: archers, longbowmen, crossbowmen, skirmishers
- Cavalry: horse archers, lancers, heavy knights
- Siege: catapult, trebuchet, ballista, ram, siege tower
- Special: war dogs, monks, banner bearers, mercenaries
- Soft counter system: spearmen > cavalry > archers > infantry > spearmen, driven by stats

Combat mechanics
- Stats: health, attack, armor, charge bonus, speed, range, accuracy, discipline, stamina
- Morale: casualties, flanking, rear attacks, general death, fatigue, terrain
- Routing and rallying, pursuit
- Flanking/rear bonuses, charge impact, formation collision
- Terrain: high ground, forest cover, rivers, mud; weather (rain lowers archer accuracy, fog lowers vision)
- Ammo, fatigue, friendly fire for arrows and artillery

Sieges
- Destructible walls and gates, towers, siege weapons, boiling oil, sally-forth, capture points, fire effects

Victory: rout/destroy enemy, capture central point, or timer

=====================================
5. AI
=====================================
Campaign AI: expansion, economy, alliances, betrayal; personalities (aggressive, defensive, trader, treacherous); multi-army coordination
Battle AI: formation deployment, flanking, protecting archers, timed cavalry charges, retreat when losing, general targeting
Pathfinding: A* or flow fields with unit avoidance
Adjustable difficulty

=====================================
6. MOBILE UI / UX
=====================================
- Landscape layout, large touch targets (minimum 48dp), safe-area support for notches
- Main menu: new campaign, continue, custom battle, tutorial, settings
- Campaign HUD: top resource bar, season indicator, collapsible province/army panels, diplomacy and tech screens, event popups, end-turn button
- Battle HUD: compact unit cards (health, ammo, morale, fatigue), formation toolbar, minimap, speed controls
- Interactive tutorial, in-game encyclopedia, tooltips via long-press
- Autosave every turn, multiple save slots, resume instantly after app interruption (calls, app switching)
- Languages: English + Indonesian localization
- Settings: graphics quality (low/medium/high), battery saver (30 FPS), FPS counter, haptics, volume sliders

=====================================
7. AUDIO
=====================================
- Dynamic orchestral music (campaign calm, battle tense, victory/defeat)
- SFX: swords, shields, hooves, arrows, siege impacts, crowd shouts, wind and rain
- Compressed audio (OGG), low memory usage

=====================================
8. MOBILE PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
=====================================
- 300-1000 soldiers on screen using sprite batching, texture atlases, object pooling, and simplified crowd simulation
- LOD for distant units (merge into block sprites when zoomed out)
- Build size under 300 MB, loading under 10 seconds
- Low battery and heat usage, quality auto-scaling
- Deterministic combat calculations, seeded RNG for save/load
- Component-based architecture, event system, state machine for campaign turns
- Data-driven JSON for units, buildings, techs, events, factions
- Unit tests for combat and economy formulas
- Debug tools: god mode, spawn units, show pathing, FPS counter

=====================================
9. DEVELOPMENT ROADMAP
=====================================
Phase 1: Battle prototype (2 armies, basic units, touch selection, movement, melee/ranged, morale, pixel sprites)
Phase 2: Formations, flanking, terrain, cavalry charges, battle AI
Phase 3: Campaign map (8 provinces), army movement, end turn, recruitment
Phase 4: Economy, buildings, settlements, upkeep
Phase 5: Link campaign to battles, auto-resolve, results
Phase 6: Diplomacy, campaign AI, generals, agents
Phase 7: Sieges, tech tree, random events
Phase 8: Full map, 5 factions, balancing
Phase 9: UI polish, audio, tutorial, save/load, optimization, Android/iOS build

OUTPUT FORMAT
- Start with Phase 1 only. Provide: project structure, all code files, pixel-art sprite specs (size, palette, animation frames), setup and APK export instructions, touch controls guide, and a list of what is done vs. planned
- After each phase, wait for my \"next\"
- Explain design decisions briefly and ask me if anything is ambiguous

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Index: scripts/battle.gd
===================================================================
--- scripts/battle.gd
+++ scripts/battle.gd
@@ -218,4 +218,183 @@
 
 func _set_message(text: String) -> void:
 	help_message = text
 	message_timer = 3.2
+
+func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if event is InputEventScreenTouch:
+		var touch := event as InputEventScreenTouch
+		if touch.pressed:
+			touch_positions[touch.index] = touch.position
+			if touch_positions.size() == 1:
+				_pointer_down(touch.position, touch.index)
+		else:
+			touch_positions.erase(touch.index)
+			_pointer_up(touch.position, touch.index)
+	elif event is InputEventScreenDrag:
+		var drag := event as InputEventScreenDrag
+		if touch_positions.size() >= 2:
+			var ids: Array = touch_positions.keys()
+			var old_a: Vector2 = touch_positions[ids[0]]
+			var old_b: Vector2 = touch_positions[ids[1]]
+			touch_positions[drag.index] = drag.position
+			var new_a: Vector2 = touch_positions[ids[0]]
+			var new_b: Vector2 = touch_positions[ids[1]]
+			var old_distance := old_a.distance_to(old_b)
+			var new_distance := new_a.distance_to(new_b)
+			if old_distance > 1.0:
+				var old_zoom := zoom
+				zoom = clampf(zoom * new_distance / old_distance, 0.78, 1.3)
+				var old_center := (old_a + old_b) * 0.5
+				var new_center := (new_a + new_b) * 0.5
+				camera_offset = new_center - (old_center - camera_offset) * (zoom / old_zoom)
+			queue_redraw()
+		else:
+			touch_positions[drag.index] = drag.position
+			drag_current = drag.position
+	elif event is InputEventMouseButton and event.pressed:
+		_pointer_down(event.position, 0)
+	elif event is InputEventMouseButton and not event.pressed:
+		_pointer_up(event.position, 0)
+	elif event is InputEventMouseMotion and dragging_unit:
+		drag_current = event.position
+
+func _pointer_down(pos: Vector2, pointer_id: int) -> void:
+	drag_id = pointer_id
+	drag_start = pos
+	drag_current = pos
+	dragging_unit = false
+	if game_over:
+		if Rect2(490, 415, 300, 70).has_point(pos):
+			_start_battle()
+		return
+	if _handle_ui(pos):
+		return
+	if not _in_field(pos):
+		return
+	var world := _screen_to_world(pos)
+	var hit := _unit_at(world)
+	if not hit.is_empty() and int(hit["team"]) == 0:
+		selected_id = str(hit["id"])
+		dragging_unit = true
+		queue_redraw()
+
+func _pointer_up(pos: Vector2, pointer_id: int) -> void:
+	if pointer_id != drag_id or game_over:
+		return
+	if dragging_unit and drag_start.distance_to(pos) > 18.0 and _in_field(pos):
+		_issue_move(_screen_to_world(pos))

# Crown & Banner: Ashes of Veyr

**Phase 1 — playable battle prototype** for Godot 4. A touch-first, landscape real-time battle between the Grey March and the Red Fen. All current battlefield graphics are original, code-drawn pixel-style placeholders; no third-party art, audio, or game assets are used.

> This repository currently implements Phase 1 only. It is a small, playable prototype, not yet the full grand-strategy game described in the longer roadmap.

## Run it

1. Install **Godot 4.2 or newer** (standard build; no plugins or imported assets required).
2. Open Godot Project Manager → **Import** and select this folder's `project.godot`.
3. Press **F6** to run the current scene or **F5** to launch the project.
4. On desktop, mouse input mirrors touch for development. The game itself has no keyboard-dependent controls.

The project uses Godot's **GL Compatibility** renderer and a 1280×720 landscape canvas, stretched to the device viewport.

## Phase 1 gameplay

- Two opposing armies, each with four regiments: spearmen, archers, heavy infantry, and cavalry.
- Regiment selection, tap-to-order movement, drag-to-move, target tapping, attack/hold/charge/fire-at-will orders, and rally.
- Real-time deterministic-seed combat simulation, melee and ranged damage, ammunition, morale, routing and rallying, retreat, and battle outcome.
- Battle pause, half-speed, 1×/2× speed, touch-friendly unit cards and order buttons, and a compact battle autosave record.
- Original procedural battlefield details, unit silhouettes, faction colors, banners, morale bars, and battle HUD.

## Touch controls

| Gesture / button | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tap a friendly regiment / unit card | Select it |
| Tap open battlefield | Move selected unit to that point |
| Drag from a friendly regiment | Move it to the drag destination |
| Tap an enemy regiment | Order the selected unit to engage |
| **ATTACK** | Engage nearest enemy |
| **HOLD** | Hold position; engage nearby attackers |
| **CHARGE** | Close with a temporary charge-speed boost |
| **FIRE AT WILL** | Missile regiment engages at range (melee units fall back to attack) |
| **RALLY** | Restore some selected regiment morale |
| **Ⅱ / ▶** | Pause or resume |
| **SLOW** | Set simulation to half speed |
| **SPEED** | Toggle 1× and 2× |
| Two-finger pinch / drag | Zoom and move the view |

All key buttons are at least 48×48 logical pixels. Desktop mouse controls are included only as a convenient development/testing fallback.

## Project structure

```text
project.godot          Godot project settings, landscape viewport, mobile renderer
scenes/main.tscn       Main battle scene
scripts/battle.gd      Battle setup, touch input, simulation, drawing, and HUD
 data/units.json       Data-driven regiment templates and combat stats
```

(The actual data directory is `data/`.) The core prototype intentionally uses one scene script to keep Phase 1 immediately runnable; combat data is separate in JSON. As later phases add campaign systems, logic will be split into reusable components and data files.

## Pixel-art placeholder specs

The prototype draws its sprites from pixel-aligned rectangles, rather than shipping raster sprite sheets. This keeps all placeholder art replaceable and avoids licensing or import setup.

- **Logical sprite cell:** 16×24 pixels per foot soldier; 24×24 horse and rider silhouette. Rendered with nearest-neighbor-style hard edges.
- **Formation rendering:** a regiment is represented by 20 tiny soldier silhouettes; its card shows the full in-world regiment size (32–48 soldiers).
- **Palette:** muted earth/field colors (`#657757`, `#76664e`), steel and linen (`#a99e84`, `#ddd0ae`), and two faction cloths (Grey March blue-grey, Red Fen dark red). Each unit uses a small subset of the palette.
- **Distinct silhouettes:** spears have a long upright spear; archers carry a bow/quiver shape; infantry carry a sword; cavalry appear mounted. Faction standards and colors distinguish sides.
- **Animation:** currently static formation poses with real-time positional movement, impact flash, and routing behavior. Actual 8-direction idle/walk/run/attack/block/hit/death/rout sprite sheets are planned, not implemented.
- **Lighting/weather/audio:** static ambient field shading only. Dynamic lighting, seasons, particles, weather, music and SFX are planned.

For production art, replace the drawing helpers in `scripts/battle.gd` with an atlas (e.g. 128×192 per 8-direction/8-action character sheet, 16×24 frame cells) using nearest filtering. The current primitives are intentionally not represented as finished high-resolution pixel art.

## Android APK / AAB export

1. In Godot, install the matching **Export Templates** (Editor → Manage Export Templates).
2. Install Android Studio / Android SDK and configure Godot's Editor Settings → **Export → Android** with the SDK path and Java SDK path. Use the JDK version recommended by the Godot version in use.
3. Project → **Export** → Add… → **Android**. For a test build, configure the debug keystore if requested, then choose **Export Project** and save an `.apk`.
4. For Play Store distribution, enable **Runnable** as appropriate, configure a release keystore/signing credentials in the Android preset, and export an `.aab` (Godot 4 Android preset supports Gradle build options; use the format selector in the export dialog).
5. Keep orientation landscape; the project requests landscape via `window/handheld/orientation`. Test touch input and safe-area behavior on-device before release.

Export settings and Android SDK UI can vary slightly across Godot 4.x releases. The preset's validation messages identify missing SDK components. iOS export requires macOS and Xcode; add an iOS preset in Godot, configure signing/team settings, export the Xcode project, then build/sign from Xcode. This environment has no Godot executable or mobile signing toolchain, so APK/iOS artifacts have not been generated here.

## Save data

After a battle ends, a compact outcome record is written to `user://battle_autosave.json` (Godot's per-user application data folder). The current Phase 1 prototype does not yet restore a full in-progress battle or expose multiple slots.

## Validation

The project files and JSON are intended for Godot 4.x. The GDScript has been formatted and parsed with `gdformat`; this environment does not include the Godot engine, so a native engine run and APK build could not be verified here.

## Done vs planned

**Done in Phase 1:** playable 2-army battle; data-driven initial regiment stats; touch/mouse selection and movement; basic melee/ranged combat; morale, rout, rally; command buttons; speed/pause controls; original code-drawn art and responsive HUD.

**Planned for later phases:** formations and unit avoidance; flanking/terrain/weather; improved battle AI and pathfinding; campaign/provinces/economy/diplomacy/technology; siege battles; detailed animation atlases and audio; tutorial/localization/settings; save slots and resume; performance profiling and signed Android/iOS builds.

## Original setting

Veyr is a fictional continent. The Grey March keeps the river roads with disciplined spearmen and a blue-grey banner. The Red Fen's warbands answer with iron discipline, field bows, and dark-red standards. The setting, names, UI, and current art are original to this prototype.

func _initialize() -> void:
	var content := FileAccess.get_file_as_string("res://data/units.json")
	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(content)
	assert(parsed is Dictionary)
	assert(parsed.has("units"))
	var templates: Array = parsed["units"]
	assert(templates.size() == 8)
	var team_totals := [0, 0]
	for index in range(templates.size()):
		var unit: Dictionary = templates[index]
		assert(int(unit["count"]) > 0)
		assert(int(unit["attack"]) > 0)
		assert(int(unit["armor"]) >= 0)
		assert(int(unit["morale"]) in range(0, 101))
		if int(unit["range"]) > 0:
			assert(int(unit["ammo"]) > 0)
		team_totals[0 if index < 4 else 1] += int(unit["count"])
	assert(team_totals[0] > 0 and team_totals[1] > 0)
	print("Phase 1 unit-data smoke test passed: ", team_totals)
	quit()

1: # Crown & Banner: Ashes of Veyr
2: 
3: **Phase 1 — playable battle prototype** for Godot 4. A touch-first, landscape real-time battle between the Grey March and the Red Fen. All current battlefield graphics are original, code-drawn pixel-style placeholders; no third-party art, audio, or game assets are used.
4: 
5: > This repository currently implements Phase 1 only. It is a small, playable prototype, not yet the full grand-strategy game described in the longer roadmap.
6: 
7: ## Run it
8: 
9: 1. Install **Godot 4.2 or newer** (standard build; no plugins or imported assets required).
10: 2. Open Godot Project Manager → **Import** and select this folder's `project.godot`.
11: 3. Press **F6** to run the current scene or **F5** to launch the project.
12: 4. On desktop, mouse input mirrors touch for development. The game itself has no keyboard-dependent controls.
13: 
14: The project uses Godot's **GL Compatibility** renderer and a 1280×720 landscape canvas, stretched to the device viewport.
15: 
16: ## Phase 1 gameplay
17: 
18: - Two opposing armies, each with four regiments: spearmen, archers, heavy infantry, and cavalry.
19: - Regiment selection, tap-to-order movement, drag-to-move, target tapping, attack/hold/charge/fire-at-will orders, and rally.
20: - Real-time deterministic-seed combat simulation, melee and ranged damage, ammunition, morale, routing and rallying, retreat, and battle outcome.
21: - Battle pause, half-speed, 1×/2× speed, touch-friendly unit cards and order buttons, and a compact battle autosave record.
22: - Original procedural battlefield details, unit silhouettes, faction colors, banners, morale bars, and battle HUD.
23: 
24: ## Touch controls
25: 
26: | Gesture / button | Action |
27: | --- | --- |
28: | Tap a friendly regiment / unit card | Select it |
29: | Tap open battlefield | Move selected unit to that point |
30: | Drag from a friendly regiment | Move it to the drag destination |
31: | Tap an enemy regiment | Order the selected unit to engage |
32: | **ATTACK** | Engage nearest enemy |
33: | **HOLD** | Hold position; engage nearby attackers |
34: | **CHARGE** | Close with a temporary charge-speed boost |
35: | **FIRE AT WILL** | Missile regiment engages at range (melee units fall back to attack) |
36: | **RALLY** | Restore some selected regiment morale |
37: | **Ⅱ / ▶** | Pause or resume |
38: | **SLOW** | Set simulation to half speed |
39: | **SPEED** | Toggle 1× and 2× |
40: | Two-finger pinch / drag | Zoom and move the view |
41: 
42: All key buttons are at least 48×48 logical pixels. Desktop mouse controls are included only as a convenient development/testing fallback.
43: 
44: ## Project structure
45: 
46: ```text
47: project.godot          Godot project settings, landscape viewport, mobile renderer
48: scenes/main.tscn       Main battle scene
49: scripts/battle.gd      Battle setup, touch input, simulation, drawing, and HUD
50: data/units.json         Data-driven regiment templates and combat stats
51: tests/combat_smoke_test.gd  Headless check for unit data and battle assumptions
52: ```
53: 
54: (The actual data directory is `data/`.) The core prototype intentionally uses one scene script to keep Phase 1 immediately runnable; combat data is separate in JSON. As later phases add campaign systems, logic will be split into reusable components and data files.
55: 
56: ## Pixel-art placeholder specs
57: 
58: The prototype draws its sprites from pixel-aligned rectangles, rather than shipping raster sprite sheets. This keeps all placeholder art replaceable and avoids licensing or import setup.
59: 
60: - **Logical sprite cell:** 16×24 pixels per foot soldier; 24×24 horse and rider silhouette. Rendered with nearest-neighbor-style hard edges.
61: - **Formation rendering:** a regiment is represented by 20 tiny soldier silhouettes; its card shows the full in-world regiment size (32–48 soldiers).
62: - **Palette:** muted earth/field colors (`#657757`, `#76664e`), steel and linen (`#a99e84`, `#ddd0ae`), and two faction cloths (Grey March blue-grey, Red Fen dark red). Each unit uses a small subset of the palette.
63: - **Distinct silhouettes:** spears have a long upright spear; archers carry a bow/quiver shape; infantry carry a sword; cavalry appear mounted. Faction standards and colors distinguish sides.
64: - **Animation:** currently static formation poses with real-time positional movement, impact flash, and routing behavior. Actual 8-direction idle/walk/run/attack/block/hit/death/rout sprite sheets are planned, not implemented.
65: - **Lighting/weather/audio:** static ambient field shading only. Dynamic lighting, seasons, particles, weather, music and SFX are planned.
66: 
67: For production art, replace the drawing helpers in `scripts/battle.gd` with an atlas (e.g. 128×192 per 8-direction/8-action character sheet, 16×24 frame cells) using nearest filtering. The current primitives are intentionally not represented as finished high-resolution pixel art.
68: 
69: ## Android APK / AAB export
70: 
71: 1. In Godot, install the matching **Export Templates** (Editor → Manage Export Templates).
72: 2. Install Android Studio / Android SDK and configure Godot's Editor Settings → **Export → Android** with the SDK path and Java SDK path. Use the JDK version recommended by the Godot version in use.
73: 3. Project → **Export** → Add… → **Android**. For a test build, configure the debug keystore if requested, then choose **Export Project** and save an `.apk`.
74: 4. For Play Store distribution, enable **Runnable** as appropriate, configure a release keystore/signing credentials in the Android preset, and export an `.aab` (Godot 4 Android preset supports Gradle build options; use the format selector in the export dialog).
75: 5. Keep orientation landscape; the project requests landscape via `window/handheld/orientation`. Test touch input and safe-area behavior on-device before release.
76: 
77: Export settings and Android SDK UI can vary slightly across Godot 4.x releases. The preset's validation messages identify missing SDK components. iOS export requires macOS and Xcode; add an iOS preset in Godot, configure signing/team settings, export the Xcode project, then build/sign from Xcode. This environment has no Godot executable or mobile signing toolchain, so APK/iOS artifacts have not been generated here.
78: 
79: ## Save data
80: 
81: After a battle ends, a compact outcome record is written to `user://battle_autosave.json` (Godot's per-user application data folder). The current Phase 1 prototype does not yet restore a full in-progress battle or expose multiple slots.
82: 
83: ## Validation
84: 
85: The project files and JSON are intended for Godot 4.x. The GDScript has been formatted and parsed with `gdformat`; this environment does not include the Godot engine, so a native engine run and APK build could not be verified here.
86: 
87: ## Done vs planned
88: 
89: **Done in Phase 1:** playable 2-army battle; data-driven initial regiment stats; touch/mouse selection and movement; basic melee/ranged combat; morale, rout, rally; command buttons; speed/pause controls; original code-drawn art and responsive HUD.
90: 
91: **Planned for later phases:** formations and unit avoidance; flanking/terrain/weather; improved battle AI and pathfinding; campaign/provinces/economy/diplomacy/technology; siege battles; detailed animation atlases and audio; tutorial/localization/settings; save slots and resume; performance profiling and signed Android/iOS builds.
92: 
93: ## Original setting
94: 
95: Veyr is a fictional continent. The Grey March keeps the river roads with disciplined spearmen and a blue-grey banner. The Red Fen's warbands answer with iron discipline, field bows, and dark-red standards. The setting, names, UI, and current art are original to this prototype.
